subject: physics

moments.title: Einstein's cosmological constant
moments.body: Applying GR to the universe, Einstein finds it must be expanding or contracting. He adds a term Lambda to keep it static. After Hubble shows expansion, he calls Lambda his 'biggest blunder'.
moments.takeaway: Einstein invents dark energy in 1917 and rejects it in 1929. He was right the first time.

moments.title: Two supernova teams
moments.who: Saul Perlmutter (LBL); Brian Schmidt, Adam Riess (Harvard/Mt Stromlo)
moments.body: Two competing teams use Type Ia supernovae — 'standardisable candles' — to measure the universe's expansion at large distances. The aim is to measure the deceleration of expansion due to gravity.
moments.takeaway: Two rival teams race to measure cosmic deceleration.

moments.title: Acceleration discovered
moments.body: Both teams find the universe's expansion is accelerating, not decelerating. Distant supernovae are dimmer than expected. Something — 'dark energy' — is pushing the universe apart. Perlmutter, Schmidt and Riess share the 2011 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: 68% of the universe is mysterious. Einstein's 'blunder' returns.

moments.title: DESI hints at evolving dark energy
moments.body: DESI's results show possible evolution of the dark-energy equation of state — at 2-4 sigma. If confirmed, the simple cosmological constant model is wrong.
moments.takeaway: Dark energy may not be a constant after all.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Dark energy makes up 68% of the universe. Its nature is unknown. Euclid (launched 2023), Roman Space Telescope (2027) and Vera Rubin Observatory will refine measurements.
now.open_questions: Is dark energy the cosmological constant or something dynamic? Why is its value so small?

reflection: Einstein called Lambda his biggest blunder. The 2011 Nobel essentially restored it. Can you be wrong about being wrong?
